subject: Re: SOC 2 scope: Azure managed services, subservice carve-out & audit period
messages:
From: Bright Assurance <auditor@brightassurance.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karen Liu <karen@elmbank.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 inquiry: Azure-managed subservice scope and audit period overlap

Hi Naomi,

We're preparing Elm Bank's SOC 2 Type II evidence package and need to confirm how Redwood is mapping Azure-managed components into your subservice organization carve-out. Specifically: 

- For the audit period 2024-10-01 to 2025-03-31, does Redwood treat Azure PaaS services (App Service, SQL DB, Blob Storage) as within scope of Redwood's SOC 2 report or as a carve-out relying on Azure's SOC reports?
- Are there any third-party subprocessors layered under Azure (e.g., CDN providers, managed DB connectors) that Elm Bank relies on which are NOT covered by Azure's SOC 2?
- If Redwood intends to rely on Azure's SOC, would you provide a bridge letter (or confirm the mechanism) that ties Azure's control coverage to Redwood's control responsibilities for the audit period above?

Please include any artifacts (mapping matrix, bridge-letter draft, or vendor attestations) you have. Elm Bank's auditor would like these by 2025-06-27 to finalize their testing plan.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Engagement Manager, Bright Assurance

---
Attachments referenced: none in original email
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Bright Assurance <auditor@brightassurance.com>; Karen Liu <karen@elmbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 inquiry: Azure-managed subservice scope and audit period overlap

Hi Maya / Karen,

Thanks for the clear questions. Quick summary up front: Redwood relies on Azure's SOC 2 Type II for core managed platform controls (PaaS compute, managed SQL, blob storage) for the 2024-10-01 to 2025-03-31 period, but there are two important caveats: 1) some optional third-party features that customers can enable (third-party CDN, certain connectors) are handled by separate subprocessors; and 2) we maintain responsibility for our application-level encryption, key custody configuration, and customer-specific tenant controls.

I attached a draft mapping table (redwood_subservice_matrix_20250620.csv) that shows which Azure services we consider covered by Azure's SOC vs controls we retain. Also attaching a short Azure SOC summary we use for customer reviews (azure-soc-summary-2024.pdf).

Next steps we propose:
- I'll coordinate an initial bridge-letter draft for Elm Bank that states Redwood's reliance on Azure for the listed platform controls and clarifies Redwood's retained responsibilities.
- Rishi will confirm the list of any non-Azure subprocessors that need separate attestation.
- Vivek / Legal will confirm whether we can sign a bridge letter or whether we should provide attestation plus supplemental evidence instead.

Can you confirm the auditor's acceptance of relying on Azure's SOC with a Redwood bridge letter? If yes, we'll aim to deliver the draft by 2025-06-24.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Compliance (Sales Org Liaison)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subservice_matrix_20250620.csv, azure-soc-summary-2024.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Bright Assurance <auditor@brightassurance.com>
Cc: Karen Liu <karen@elmbank.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 inquiry: Azure-managed subservice scope and audit period overlap

Thanks Naomi — adding technical detail.

Notes from infra mapping: 
- Azure PaaS: App Service (web app) + Azure SQL Managed Instance + Blob Storage = covered by Azure's SOC for infrastructure & platform controls (networking, VM host, hypervisor, physical).
- Our configuration: we enable customer-managed keys (CMK) for Elm Bank in Azure Key Vault. Key custody is customer-facing; Redwood uses Azure Key Vault 'BYOK' binding but does not export keys. That responsibility remains with Elm Bank (they hold the HSM/KMS keys).
- Subprocessors: we use FastEdge CDN for static assets delivery in some regions (opt-in). FastEdge is NOT covered by Azure SOC; we've included FastEdge as a subprocessor in the matrix where applicable.
- Connectors: a managed DB-replication connector operated by DbBridge Inc. is only used by <5% of tenants; it's listed as a subprocessor and requires separate attestation.

I'll attach the technical appendix to the matrix showing how we tie controls (change control, encryption, network segmentation) to Azure's control IDs.

Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: technical_appendix_for_matrix.pdf (included in internal folder)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Bright Assurance <auditor@brightassurance.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 inquiry: Azure-managed subservice scope and audit period overlap

Naomi / team — legal / procurement weigh-in.

We can provide a bridge letter that: (a) identifies the Azure SOC report we rely on (SOC 2 Type II report for Azure covering 2024-09-01 to 2025-03-31), (b) states the specific control areas Redwood delegates to Azure (platform availability, host/hypervisor, physical security), and (c) explicitly lists retained responsibilities (application-level encryption, key custody, customer onboarding procedures, patch cadence for app code).

However, for subprocessors that are not covered by Azure (FastEdge, DbBridge Inc.), we cannot reference Azure's SOC; instead, we can: 
- provide the subprocessors' SOC/attestation if available, or
- provide evidence of compensating controls (network ACLs, WAF rules, S3 signed URLs) that reduce the auditor's risk assessment.

I drafted a short bridge letter template (draft_bridge_letter_naomi_v1.docx). If Elm Bank's auditor accepts this format I recommend: finalizing and sending it with the matrix and the subprocessor list by 2025-06-24.

Vivek
VP, Legal & Business Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_bridge_letter_naomi_v1.docx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Bright Assurance <auditor@brightassurance.com>, Karen Liu <karen@elmbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 inquiry: Azure-managed subservice scope and audit period overlap

Maya / Karen — next steps and deliverables.

Thanks for the patience while we compiled the mapping. Per above conversation, please find attached:
- redwood_subservice_matrix_20250620.csv (mapping of services and subprocessors)
- draft_bridge_letter_naomi_v1.docx (bridge letter template referencing Azure SOC and Redwood retained controls)
- azure-soc-summary-2024.pdf (executive summary of Azure SOC coverage)

Summary of decisions we propose: 
1) Elm Bank auditor may rely on Azure's SOC 2 Type II for platform controls for the audit period 2024-10-01 to 2025-03-31, provided Bright Assurance accepts the attached bridge letter as tying Azure's controls to Redwood's responsibilities.
2) For non-Azure subprocessors (FastEdge, DbBridge Inc.), Redwood will either obtain the subprocessor's attestation or provide compensating control evidence; we will deliver that evidence by 2025-06-30 if requested.
3) Key custody: Elm Bank retains control of CMKs; Redwood documents this in the matrix and the bridge letter.

Please confirm whether the bridge letter format is acceptable and whether Bright Assurance needs any additional artifact (e.g., signed subprocessor attestations, configuration snapshots). We'll queue a DocuSign envelope if you want a signed bridge letter.

Best regards,
Naomi
Head of Compliance (Sales Org Liaison)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subservice_matrix_20250620.csv, draft_bridge_letter_naomi_v1.docx, azure-soc-summary-2024.pdf
